Abstract
Large Language Models (LLMs) encounter significant performance bottlenecks
in long-sequence tasks due to the computational complexity and memory over-
head inherent in the self-attention mechanism. To address these challenges, we
introduce ALLMEM, a novel and efficient hybrid architecture that integrates Slid-
ing Window Attention (SWA) with non-linear Test-Time Training (TTT) memory
networks. ALLMEM enables models to effectively scale to ultra-long contexts
while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. This approach not only overcomes the
representation constraints typical of linear memory models but also significantly
reduces the computational and memory footprint during long-sequence inference. Furthermore, we implement a Memory-Efficient Fine-Tuning strategy to replace
standard attention layers in pre-trained models with memory-augmented sliding
window layers. This framework facilitates the efficient transformation of any off-
the-shelf pre-trained LLM into an ALLMEM-based architecture.

in terms of computational cost and cache storage requirements, we compare the number of floating-

lengths. In the experiments, the sliding-window size is fixed at 4096, and the update chunk size

The memory processing mechanisms of AllMem and MSA differ in terms of computational complexity during inference as follows:

- **AllMem**: The ALLMEM architecture achieves a significant reduction in computational cost and cache storage requirements compared to the full-attention mechanism. Specifically, when the context length extends to 128k, the computational cost and cache storage requirement of the ALLMEM model are reduced to approximately 1/9 of those of the full-attention mechanism. The cache capacity of the ALLMEM model remains constant regardless of sequence length, which contrasts with the full-attention layer that grows linearly with sequence length.

- **MSA**: The Memory Sparse Attention (MSA) achieves linear computational complexity with respect to memory size L during inference, specifically O(L) efficiency. This allows MSA to maintain consistent performance while processing large memory banks, with minimal degradation in quality across varying context lengths.

In summary, ALLMEM reduces computational costs significantly compared to full attention, while MSA maintains linear complexity with respect to memory size, allowing for efficient processing during inference.
